# Heroes next door: Meet three members of Team Robinson lifting up their communities


#### Through Robinson Heroes, employees recognize colleagues who bring their time, talents and heart to communities around the world.


-
-
-
-
- Copy to clipboard


Copy to clipboard


Link Copied


2026-11-19 | News


What does a hero look like? At C.H. Robinson, it might be someone planting a school garden, planning a community retreat, or turning a team celebration into a chance to give back.


Those are the kinds of stories behind Robinson Heroes, an employee recognition program from the C.H. Robinson Foundation that celebrates teammates who make a meaningful difference in their communities outside their day-to-day roles. Employees around the world nominate colleagues whose volunteer service, leadership, fundraising, or advocacy deserves a little more of the spotlight.


The program began as part of the Foundation’s 20th anniversary celebration last year. The idea was simple: ask employees who inspires them. The response made one thing clear—there is no shortage of teammates across C.H. Robinson who bring the same care, creativity and follow-through they show for customers to the communities they call home.


Three recent honorees, Allison Gaubatz, Roxana Vargas and Matthias Abraham, show just how many forms that impact can take.


## Allison Gaubatz helps students grow


Allison Gaubatz, a Commercial Development Representative based in the United States, has spent years volunteering with the Lebanon Community Unit School District in Illinois, including service on its Board of Education and as board president.


Her community résumé is not exactly short. She has helped create Kids Career Day experiences that introduce students to entrepreneurship, leadership and business. Through the Booster Club, she develops fundraising ideas that help more young people participate in extracurricular and athletic programs. She also advocates for students and families at City Council and Chamber of Commerce meetings, including efforts to improve pedestrian access and crosswalk safety.


And then there is the school garden. What began with soil and seeds grew into a hands-on classroom for nutrition, sustainability and responsibility. For Allison, who has more than 20 years of experience as an educator, learning is not limited to a desk—and opportunity should not be limited by a child’s circumstances.


“Her goal is simple but powerful: ensuring that every child, regardless of circumstances, has the chance to participate, learn and succeed,” said Raquel Rife, Allison’s nominator and longtime friend.


## Roxana Vargas turns showing up into an art form


Roxana Vargas does not simply volunteer. She brings the plan, coordinates the people and creates ways for others to get involved.


An Account Manager in San Antonio, Texas, Roxana contributes hundreds of volunteer hours each year through her church, the Society of St. Vincent de Paul, the San Antonio Transportation Association and other local outreach efforts. Whether she is organizing an event, coordinating volunteers, supporting fundraising or helping shape a community program, she has a talent for turning good intentions into meaningful action.


One example is the Society of St. Vincent de Paul’s annual retreat at the Schoenstatt Marian Shrine in Helotes, Texas. As retreat chair, Roxana helped guide the event from idea to execution—coordinating speakers, activities, logistics and volunteers for a day centered on fellowship, personal growth and service. It is one expression of the broader leadership she brings to organizations across her community.


“Service is not something she does occasionally; it is part of who she is,” said her manager and nominator, Matt Persyn. “She leads not for recognition, but because she believes in making a difference.”


## Matthias Abraham makes giving back a team sport


For Matthias Abraham, Senior Manager of Global Forwarding Pricing in Austria, team spirit can travel well beyond the office.


Across the European Pricing team, Matthias has connected team-building and recognition activities with charitable giving and community support. He helps organize initiatives, builds enthusiasm and creates ways for colleagues to participate together—showing that shared success can also create shared impact.


“Rather than focusing solely on business achievements, he created opportunities for the team to contribute to broader social causes,” said Maryna Andriychuk, who nominated Matthias. “His actions show a commitment to fostering both a high-performing and socially conscious team culture.”


Allison, Roxana and Matthias serve different communities in different ways, but their stories share a common thread: they notice where they can help, bring others along and follow through.


“None of these stories starts with someone looking for the spotlight,” said Rachel Schwalbach. “They start with someone seeing a need, rolling up their sleeves and bringing others along. That’s Team Robinson at its best—and it’s how our people make a real difference in communities around the world.”


Robinson Heroes gives those efforts a name and a well-earned moment of recognition. More importantly, it reveals something about the people behind a global logistics company: long after the workday ends, many are still solving problems, creating connections and helping their communities move forward.


[Learn more](https://www.chrobinson.com/en-us/about-us/corporate-responsibility/community/) about how Team Robinson supports communities.
